en.quote: Over the course of a decade, we must at least double the country’s gross domestic product.
en.head: Real GDP rose by roughly half over the following decade.
en.body: The World Bank’s constant-price series puts Russian GDP at about $921 billion in 2003 and $1.38 trillion in 2013: roughly 50% growth, rather than 100%. Later claims that it had “almost doubled” used 2000 as the starting year and a longer period; they do not test the decade starting in 2003.
